title: observability pipeline debug notes - trace/metrics/logs drop (Maya)
content:
Summary:
- Brief: sudden drop in traces + metrics and backlog growth for log ingestion starting ~2024-11-12T03:40Z. Hosted customers experienced missing spans; internal dashboards show metrics delta = -60% for service ingress. Logs queued in kafka topic obs-raw-logs increased from normal ~200k to ~1.2M.

Observed symptoms & quick timeline:
- 03:35Z: anomaly detection alert for metric ingestion drop (alerts/metric-ingestion-low).
- 03:40Z: traces sampled per-second on frontend team drop by ~70%.
- 03:45Z: logs ingestion lag alarm (kafka consumer lag > 1M messages).
- 03:50Z: first 5 customer tickets report missing traces in UI.
- 04:05Z: internal slack thread created (#observability) and paging to on-call.

What I saw (raw outputs / snippets):
- kafka-consumer-groups --bootstrap-server kafka-01:9092 --describe --group obs-ingest-group
  "TOPIC           PARTITION  CURRENT-OFFSET  LOG-END-OFFSET  LAG             CONSUMER-ID              HOST            CLIENT-ID"
  "obs-raw-logs    3          1452367          1452367         1000000         consumer-obs-1            /10.3.4.12      obs-processor-1"

- obsctl tail --service ingest --since 10m | rg ERROR -n
  "2024-11-12T03:43:51Z ERROR ingestion.worker Failed to decode message: AvroDeserializationException: missing required field 'trace_id' in record"
  "2024-11-12T03:44:12Z WARN  ingestion.queue Processing delay > 30s for 3000 messages"

- kubectl get pods -n obs-ingest
  "NAME                                  READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE"
  "ingest-worker-0                       1/1     Running   0          8d"
  "ingest-worker-1                       0/1     CrashLoopBackOff  12   2h"

- kubectl logs ingest-worker-1 -n obs-ingest | tail -n 50 (excerpt)
  "panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference"
  "goroutine 83 [running]:\n  github.com/redwood-inference/obs-ingest/processor.processMessage(0xc0005a4f00)\n\thome/runner/work/obs-ingest/processor/worker.go:214 +0x5d3"

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Recent serialization change in producer introduced nullable trace_id (Avro schema mismatch) -> downstream AvroDeserializationException and panic when code assumes non-nil trace_id. (high)
2) Memory leak / OOMs on one ingestion node leading to CrashLoopBackOff and partial consumer group membership -> uneven processing and backlog. (medium)
3) Network flakiness to the metadata service (schema-registry) causing temporary inability to fetch latest schema -> fallback behaviour causing decoding errors. (low)
4) A config rollout (feature flag: "strip-empty-trace-ids") accidentally enabled in canary and pushed to ingest workers. (medium)

Commands / checks tried and results:
- Checked schema-registry for latest Avro schema for topic obs-raw-logs:
  curl -s http://schema-registry:8081/subjects/obs-raw-logs-value/versions/latest | jq .
  -> shows field trace_id {"type":"string"} in schema v14 (no optional).
- Queried recent commits to producer repo around 03:30Z:
  gh api repos/redwood-inference/log-producer/commits --since 2024-11-12T00:00:00Z | jq '.[0:10]'
  -> found a commit "add support for nullable trace_id" by user 'dev-robot' at 2024-11-12T02:58Z (PR merged 03:10Z).
- Inspecting the producer artifact deployed on staging and prod: prod image tag log-producer:sha-9f2e. Diff shows 'trace_id' now annotated as nullable in code (line reference).
- Replayed a sample message from the topic into a local consumer with avro-deserializer: example message shows null "trace_id": {"trace_id": null, "span_id":"..."}.
  -> deserialization failed in our consumer but producer schema mismatch exists.
- Rolled forward a local patch (quick-fix) adding defensive nil-check in processor.processMessage; restarted a single worker (ingest-worker-1) in cluster as a canary.
  kubectl rollout restart deployment/ingest-worker -n obs-ingest --selector=pod=ingest-worker-1
  -> post-restart logs show fewer panics, but still AvroDeserializationException for null trace_id when using strict Avro reader.

Immediate mitigation taken so far:
- Scaled up consumer replicas by +2 to handle backlog (kubectl scale deploy/ingest-worker --replicas=5 -n obs-ingest).
- Temporarily paused low-priority producers (batch logs ingestion) via rate-limit rule in kafka (reduced incoming volume ~30%).
- Opened an incident PR to revert the producer change: GH PR #876 (linked). Team asked to hold further producer deploys until fix consensus.

Open experiments / next steps:
- Short-term: coordinate with producer team to either reintroduce non-nullable trace_id or publish a compatible schema (update consumer to accept union ["null","string"]). Producer to revert if agreed. (Owner: Priya)
- Medium-term: make consumer Avro reader tolerant to nullable trace_id (update schema handling + add unit tests). (Owner: Eli)
- Add a canary gate for schema changes: automatic check on producer PRs that compares produced Avro schema with registered schema and blocks merges that change required->nullable fields without approval. (Owner: platform-eng)
- Add observability: new alert for AvroDeserializationException rate > 5/min with link to consumer pod and commit sha.

Notes for post-incident writeup:
- Root cause likely a producer-side change (03:10Z merge) that introduced nullable trace_id while registry still marked field as required; consumers assume non-null and code paths dereference trace_id causing panic; partial consumer restarts -> lag.
- Impact: some customers missing spans, traces dropped in UI, elevated latency for trace-aware features.
- Timeline artifacts: need to capture exact commit SHAs, deployment times, schema-registry version, and Kafka offset ranges for messages with null trace_id.

Questions / things to confirm:
- Was the producer schema intentionally changed to nullable? Who approved PR? Check PR history + review comments.
- Did schema-registry get updated at same time? Our check showed schema v14 still required; maybe producer used local/embedded schema.
- Are there any other fields that changed similarly? (search PR diff for Avro schema edits).

Next immediate actions (short list):
- Priya to reach out to producer on-call and request rollback OR coordinated schema update (ETA 30m).
- Eli to push a defensive consumer patch to master + release a hotfix image for ingest-worker and run as canary.
- Me (Maya) to draft incident summary and post initial notes to #observability and incident doc.

Misc notes / breadcrumbs:
- Observability alert IDs: alerts/metric-ingestion-low, alerts/kafka-lag-high, alerts/avro-deser-errors.
- Kafka topic: obs-raw-logs (partitions 0..5).
- Suspect commit: log-producer PR 332 (user dev-robot) merged 2024-11-12T03:10Z.
- Local replay command used: kafka-avro-console-consumer --bootstrap-server kafka-01:9092 --topic obs-raw-logs --from-beginning --max-messages 10 --property value.deserializer=io.confluent.kafka.serializers.KafkaAvroDeserializer

If anything else I should try quickly, add below.

[end of notes]
